sectionGalleryItems.title: Golden Hour Leopard Tracking in Block 1
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Early morning 5:00 AM entry into Yala National Park aboard our custom-built 4x4 Toyota Hilux safari jeeps.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Sri Lankan Leopard resting on granite outcrop at golden hour in Yala

sectionGalleryItems.title: Elevated 6-Seat Viewing Deck
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Forward-facing cushioned bucket seats with unobstructed 360-degree photography angles and roll-up canvas sides.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Custom 4x4 safari jeep traversing Sri Lankan national park trail

sectionGalleryItems.title: Udawalawe Wild Elephant Herd
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Multi-generational Asian elephant families gathering along the Udawalawe reservoir shoreline.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Asian elephant family walking across grasslands in Udawalawe National Park

sectionGalleryItems.title: Bundala & Kumana Coastal Wetlands
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Migratory Greater Flamingos, Painted Storks, and Bee-eaters feeding in shallow brackish lagoons.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Flock of flamingos wading in Bundala coastal lagoon at sunrise

sectionGalleryItems.title: Panthera pardus kotiya — Sri Lankan Leopard
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Yala Block 1 and Block 5 hold one of the highest leopard densities in the world.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Close-up of a Sri Lankan leopard in Yala National Park

sectionGalleryItems.title: Sri Lankan Sloth Bear During Palu Season
sectionGalleryItems.caption: May to July brings sloth bears out to feast on ripe golden Palu berries across rocky scrubland.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Sloth bear foraging in Yala forest scrub

sectionGalleryItems.title: Full-Day Bush Picnic by Menik Ganga
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Full-day safaris include freshly prepared breakfast and lunch served at shaded riverside rest stops.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Scenic golden savannah and watering hole in Yala National Park

sectionGalleryItems.title: Iconic Tuskers & Calf Herds
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Guaranteed close-range sightings of wild elephant herds grazing across open Patana grasslands.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Herd of wild elephants with calves in Udawalawe National Park

sectionGalleryItems.title: Crested Hawk-Eagle & Raptors
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Dead trees emerging from the Udawalawe reservoir serve as perches for White-bellied Sea Eagles and Changeable Hawk-Eagles.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Raptor perched on deadwood branch overlooking Udawalawe reservoir

sectionGalleryItems.title: Ramsar Wetland Sanctuary — 197+ Bird Species
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Quiet coastal lagoons hosting Greater Flamingos, Black-necked Storks, Spoonbills, and Blue-tailed Bee-eaters.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Waterbirds wading in Bundala National Park lagoon

sectionGalleryItems.title: Estuarine & Mugger Crocodiles Basking
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Both saltwater and freshwater crocodiles bask along Bundala’s sunlit sandbars and channels.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Crocodile basking on bank of Bundala lagoon

sectionGalleryItems.title: Leopard Patrol Along Natural Sand-Rimmed Villus
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Sri Lanka’s largest national park features serene natural lakes (Villus) where leopards stalk spotted deer.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Leopard walking along sandy forest track in Wilpattu National Park

sectionGalleryItems.title: Spotted Deer (Axis axis) & Ceylon Junglefowl
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Morning mist rising over Kokkare Villu with herds of spotted deer and barking deer.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Spotted deer alert in forest clearing in Wilpattu

sectionGalleryItems.title: Over 300 Elephants at Ancient Minneriya Tank
sectionGalleryItems.caption: During the dry season, herds from across the North Central Province converge on Minneriya’s receding grassy shores.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Large gathering of Asian elephants by Minneriya tank water edge

sectionGalleryItems.title: Sunset Over Minneriya Wewa
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Afternoon safaris culminate in golden silhouettes of bathing elephants and flocks of cormorants.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Elephants silhouetted against golden sunset at Minneriya reservoir

sectionGalleryItems.title: 200-Hectare Kumana Villu Nesting Sanctuary
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Thousands of Pelicans, Painted Storks, Spoonbills, and Purple Herons nest in the mangrove swamps from April to July.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Colorful kingfisher and waterbirds in Kumana National Park

sectionGalleryItems.title: Untamed Yala East Leopard & Tusker Trails
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Remote tracks along the Kumbukkan Oya river offer tranquil leopard and elephant encounters away from crowds.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Wild elephant crossing river trail in Kumana Yala East

sectionGalleryItems.title: Southern & Dry-Zone Wildlife Corridor
sectionGalleryItems.caption: We operate across Yala, Udawalawe, Bundala, Kumana, Lunugamvehera, Minneriya, Kaudulla, and Wilpattu.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Safari 4x4 jeep on scenic dry-zone wilderness track

sectionGalleryItems.title: Tailored Photography & Family Game Drives
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Whether tracking elusive leopards or watching baby elephants at play, every route is customized to the season.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Panoramic wildlife landscape in southern Sri Lanka

sectionGalleryItems.title: 15+ Years Born & Raised Beside Yala
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Deep local knowledge of animal behavior, alarm calls, and territorial tracks across all five blocks of Yala.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Safari tracker guiding guests from open-top 4x4 jeep

sectionGalleryItems.title: Ethical Wildlife Distance & Conservation First
sectionGalleryItems.caption: We respect park speed limits, never crowd resting animals, and position our jeeps thoughtfully for natural sightings.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Respectful wildlife photography of a leopard in natural habitat

sectionGalleryItems.title: Morning Mist & Golden Light in Block 1
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Captured during our 5:30 AM gate entry drive with guests from Europe and Australia.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Leopard photographed in morning golden light

sectionGalleryItems.title: Indian Peafowl Full Plumage Display
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Vibrant male peacock dancing along the Palatupana coastal track in Yala.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Peacock displaying iridescent feathers in Sri Lanka

sectionGalleryItems.title: Unforgettable Family & Private Photography Tours
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Rated 4.9/5 across Tripadvisor and Google Reviews by hundreds of international wildlife travelers.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Happy safari wildlife encounter with elephants in Sri Lanka

sectionGalleryItems.title: Complimentary Door-to-Door Hotel Pickup
sectionGalleryItems.caption: Direct 4x4 jeep pickup from hotels in Tissamaharama, Yala, Kirinda, Weerawila, Kataragama, and Hambantota.
sectionGalleryItems.alt: Safari jeep ready for morning hotel pickup in Tissamaharama
